article_content: Chiara Ferrara, a 27-year-old graduate of King's College, Cambridge, and a dedicated rower, suffered severe leg injuries after her bicycle was struck by a car in Ely, Cambridgeshire, this past May. The accident resulted in fractures to her tibia and fibula, ending her hopes of representing Great Britain in rowing—a goal she pursued as part of the Start programme, which identifies and develops future Olympic athletes. The responsible driver, Stephen Bocking, 47, from Ely, pleaded guilty to driving without due care and attention at Cambridge Magistrates' Court on October 3. He received six penalty points on his license, a £300 fine, and was ordered to pay court costs, despite the maximum sentence allowing for a £2,500 fine, more penalty points, or a driving ban. Ferrara, who works in Cambridge University's alumni relations, voiced strong disappointment at the lenient sentence and the driver’s lack of remorse. She criticized the justice system for not reflecting the profound, lasting effects such incidents have on victims. Despite doctors warning she might never run again, Ferrara remains determined to challenge that prognosis. Reflecting on her loss, Ferrara shared the heartbreak of seeing her Olympic dreams taken away by a momentary lapse in another person’s attention. She advocates for better driver education, stronger penalties, and greater awareness of the responsibilities drivers bear when on the road.

Wannan hatsari ya sa ƙashin tibia da fibula nata suka fashe, wanda hakan ya karya burinta na wakiltar Burtaniya a rowa—burin da take aikata kokari ta cimma ta hanyar shirin Start da ke horar da 'yan wasa don Gasar Olympic mai zuwa. Ta ce tsarin shari'a ba ya nuna girman tasirin da irin wannan abu ke yi a rayuwar wanda aka jikkata. England captain Wayne Rooney believes it is crucial to begin their European Championship qualifying campaign with a strong result against Switzerland. Just 76 days after their disappointing World Cup exit, England are now turning their attention to the next major tournament in France. Although escaping Group E should be manageable, manager Roy Hodgson’s squad faces their toughest match first.

Rooney, who became captain following Steven Gerrard’s retirement from international football, has been preparing the team at St George’s Park. Switzerland, ranked ninth in the world, are regarded as favorites for Monday’s game in Basel—a result England are determined to avoid.

Rooney emphasized the need for a positive start: “It’s important to begin the campaign with a good result. We should try to win, but it’s vital not to lose and give Switzerland an early advantage.”

There is understandable negativity around the England team after the World Cup. This was reflected in the low turnout at Wembley for the recent 1-0 friendly win over Norway—the lowest attendance for an international since the stadium’s 2007 reopening. The 40,181 fans who attended were also unimpressed with the uninspiring performance.

Nonetheless, Rooney is optimistic about the future, referencing the enthusiasm and attacking football England displayed against Italy in the World Cup opener, despite losing the match. “These are exciting times. Although our results against Italy and Uruguay were disappointing, I thought we played well. The players gained vital experience from the tournament.”

With the retirement of Gerrard, Frank Lampard, and Ashley Cole, and a growing list of injuries, other squad members now need to step up. In recent days, goalkeeper Ben Foster and Newcastle’s Jack Colback have withdrawn from the squad, and Daniel Sturridge suffered a thigh injury in training, returning to Liverpool for treatment. Sturridge posted his disappointment on Twitter, saying he was “heartbroken” and hoping to return soon.

Rooney is hopeful of leading by example, aiming to score and help England secure a winning start in Basel.

Kyaftin din Ingila, Wayne Rooney, ya ce yana da muhimmanci su fara wasan neman shiga gasar zakarun Turai da sakamako mai kyau a kan Switzerland. Kwanaki 76 bayan rashin nasara a gasar cin kofin duniya, Ingila ta mayar da hankali kan babban gasar kasa da kasa a Faransa. Duk da saukin ficewa daga rukuni E, tawagar Roy Hodgson za ta fara da mafi wahalar wasanninta.

Rooney, wanda ya zama kyaftin bayan Steven Gerrard ya yi ritaya daga wasan kasa da kasa, yana jagorantar atisaye a St George’s Park. Switzerland wacce ta ke ta tara a duniya, ita ce ake gani za ta fi karfin Ingila a kai wasan ranar Litinin a Basel—amma Ingila na son kauce wa faduwa.

Rooney ya ce: "Muhimmanci ne muyi kyakkyawan farawa. Ya kamata mu yi iyakar kokari don cin nasara, amma mafi mahimmanci kada mu sha kashi domin kada mu bar Switzerland ta riga mu gaba tun farko."

Akwai jin damuwa a cikin rundunar Ingila bayan fitar su daga gasar cin kofin duniya, musamman bayan karancin masu kallo a Wembley a wasan sada zumunta da Norway inda suka ci 1-0—mafi karancin mahalarta tun bayan bude filin a 2007. Masu kallo 40,181 da suka halarta ba su gamsu da wasar ba.

Sai dai, Rooney na da kyakkyawar fata game da gaba, ya tuna yadda suka taka leda da kwazo a wasan farko da Italy a gasar cin kofin duniya duk da sun sha kashi. "Wannan wani lokaci ne mai kayatarwa. Duk da rashin nasara da Italy da Uruguay, na ga munwe kokari sosai. 'Yan wasa sun kara samun kwarewa mai mahimmanci daga gasar."

Bayan ritayar Gerrard, Frank Lampard da Ashley Cole, da kuma karin raunuka, sauran ‘yan wasa za su kara tashi tsaye. Kwanakin baya, Ben Foster da Jack Colback sun janye, sai kuma Daniel Sturridge ya ji rauni a atisaye, ya koma Liverpool jinya. Sturridge ya fitar da sakon bakin ciki a Twitter, inda ya ce "na ji ciwo sosai, zan dawo nan kusa."

Rooney na fatan ya kafa kwallo kuma ya taimaka Ingila ta samu nasara a Basel.

article_content: Prince Harry was involved in a high-speed accident yesterday in central London when a police outrider from his motorcade collided head-on with a minicab. The incident occurred as the royal convoy was on its way to the Invictus Games. Prince Harry witnessed the crash and appeared visibly concerned as emergency services arrived. The police officer, a member of the Special Escort Group, was thrown about 30 feet after the collision, while the minicab driver was left unconscious and had to be freed from the vehicle by firemen. Photos showed the police motorcycle lodged in the front of a white Toyota Prius, with airbags deployed around the injured driver. A witness stated that Prince Harry's vehicle, a Range Rover, took evasive action, maneuvering carefully past the crash site under the direction of his anti-terrorism-trained driver before stopping several hundred feet down the road. Harry was reportedly distressed, closely watching the scene with clear concern for the injured parties. Both the police officer and the minicab driver were hospitalized. The officer was released later the same day; the minicab driver was reported to be in stable condition. CCTV footage reviewed by the Mail showed the minicab pulling onto the main road from a side street, colliding with the police motorcycle, which had its lights on but no sirens. The aftermath was chaotic, with debris on the road and emergency services responding quickly. After the crash, traffic was diverted for several hours while the scene was cleared. Royal aides confirmed Prince Harry was unharmed. The Metropolitan Police have launched an investigation, and no arrests have been made. The Special Escort Group, responsible for royal convoy security, consists of highly trained officers who use motorcycles with blue lights and whistles to direct London traffic. The incident is expected to prompt an internal safety review among the escort group. Sources praised the quick response of police and emergency personnel, who treated the injured until ambulances arrived.

article_content: Dicarlo Bennett, a 28-year-old baggage handler at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), has been arrested after dry ice explosions at the airport. Bennett works for Servisair and reportedly viewed the incidents as a prank, with no intention to cause harm or pursue a political motive, according to police. No injuries were reported, but the explosions prompted a brief shutdown of one terminal, which raised questions about airport security. Deputy Chief Michael Downing from the LAPD explained that Bennett regarded the explosive devices as a joke, without fully understanding the severity of putting such objects near airplanes. Bennett is charged with possessing an explosive or destructive device near an aircraft and is being held on $1 million bail. The two incidents happened on Sunday and Monday. The first involved a plastic bottle with dry ice detonating in an employee restroom in Terminal 2, leading to a temporary evacuation. On Monday, more bottles of dry ice were found in the Tom Bradley International Terminal, but only one exploded and no one was hurt. Access to both restrooms is restricted to authorized employees. Servisair, Bennett's employer, confirmed his arrest, stated their cooperation with law enforcement, and operates at over 100 sites worldwide. Airport officials have assured the public that LAX remains safe and restricted access is in place where the incidents happened. Typically, dry ice is used as a cooling agent for transporting foods like meat and ice cream. As it warms up, it changes from a solid to a gas, which can cause a build-up of pressure and result in explosions if confined.
translated_content: An kama Dicarlo Bennett, dan shekara 28, mai kula da kaya a filin jirgin sama na Los Angeles (LAX), bayan fashewar kankara mai sanyi a filin. Bennett, wanda ke aiki a Servisair, ya bayyana cewa ya dauki wannan abu a matsayin wasa ne kawai, ba tare da wata manufa ta cutarwa ko siyasa ba, kamar yadda ‘yan sanda suka ce. Babu wanda ya ji rauni, sai dai fashewar ta janyo a dakatar da aiki na ɗan lokaci a wani bangare, inda hakan ya tada batun tsaro. Shugaban ‘yan sanda Michael Downing na LAPD ya ce Bennett bai gane tsananin lamarin ba, yana daukar abun wasa ne. Ana tuhumar Bennett da mallakar na’ura mai fashewa kusa da jirgin sama kuma yana tsare da beli na dala miliyan daya. Abubuwan biyu sun faru ne ranar Lahadi da Litinin. Na farko ya faru lokacin da kwalban roba dauke da kankara mai sanyi ta fashe a bandakin ma’aikata na Terminal 2, hakan ya sa aka kwashe mutane na ɗan lokaci. A Litinin, an sake samun wasu kwalabe a Tom Bradley International Terminal, amma daya kawai ya fashe, ba kuma a samu rauni ba. Wadannan wuraren ma’aikata ne kadai ke iya shiga. Servisair, kamfanin da Bennett ke aiki, ya tabbatar da kamawa, suna kuma hada kai da hukumomi. Suna da ofisoshi sama da 100 a duniya. Hukumar kula da filin jirgin sama ta tabbatar da tsaro sannan ta bayyana cewa wurin da lamarin ya faru ma’aikata masu izini ne kadai ke iya shiga. Kankara mai sanyi (carbon dioxide daskararre) ana amfani da ita wajen kwantar da abinci a lokacin sufuri. Lokacin da ta fara dumi, tana canzawa kai tsaye zuwa iskar gas, wanda zai iya haifar da fashewa idan an kulle ta a cikin wani abu ba tare da hanyar fitan iska ba.

article_content: Recent CCTV footage from Leeds train station reveals the grave dangers people face when crossing active railway lines. In one incident, a woman prioritized retrieving her handbag over avoiding an oncoming train, but narrowly made it across. In another, a young man, apparently intoxicated, crossed the tracks and was eventually pulled to safety. Network Rail notes that almost 50 people died due to trespassing on railway tracks between April last year and March this year, with most victims being men aged 16 to 25. In response, Network Rail has launched the ‘Track Tests’ safety campaign starring 400m hurdles champion Dai Greene. Through videos and digital outreach, the campaign demonstrates that even top athletes cannot reliably avoid the dangers posed by train tracks, especially in hazardous conditions. Greene shares firsthand how railway lines pose unpredictable challenges beyond athletic ability. Social media and online ads are being used to spread the message, with a focus on reaching younger audiences. Greene, a world champion, stresses that speed and agility are no defense against the risks present on railway lines. Network Rail’s figures, excluding suicides and crossing fatalities, also cite over 400 near-miss incidents involving people rushing across tracks or attempting to retrieve belongings. The personal loss of Wendy Smith, whose 15-year-old son Ricky died on the tracks, highlights the emotional toll of these preventable accidents. Network Rail urges the public to avoid shortcuts across railway lines, emphasizing that the risks are never justified, as real stories and expert voices in the campaign attest.
translated_content: Bidiyon CCTV daga tashar jirgin kasa ta Leeds ya nuna hadarin da mutane ke fuskanta idan suka ketare layin jirgin kasa yana aiki. A wata hira, wata mata ta fi damuwa da jakarta fiye da jirgin da ke tafe, amma sai dai da kyar ta tsallake. Wani saurayi kuma, wanda ake kyautata zaton yana shan giya, ya ratsa layin kuma aka ja shi zuwa ga tsira. Kamfanin Network Rail ya bayyana cewa kimanin mutane 50 sun mutu sanadiyyar ketare layin jirgin kasa daga watan Afrilu bara zuwa watan Maris bana, yawancin su maza ne masu shekaru 16 zuwa 25. A yunkurin rage wannan matsalar, Network Rail ta kaddamar da kamfen din 'Track Tests' tare da shahararren dan wasan tsalle na mita 400, Dai Greene. Ta amfani da bidiyo da yanar-gizo, kamfen din na nuna yadda ma ƙwararrun ‘yan wasa ba za su iya kaucewa hadari a layin jirgin ba, musamman idan yanayi ba su dace ba. Greene da kansa ya bayyana yadda layin jirgin ke da haɗari fiye da yadda ake tsammani. Sako na yaduwa a kafafen sada zumunta da tallace-tallace na kan layi, musamman don isarwa ga matasa. Greene, zakara na duniya, ya jaddada cewa sauri da kwarewa kadai ba zai kare mutum daga haɗarin da ke cikin layin jirgin ba. Kididdigar Network Rail, ba tare da lissafa masu kashe kansu ko asarar rayuka a layin mota ba, ta nuna akwai fiye da kirdadon 400 da mutane suka kusan shiga hatsari bisa son dauko kaya ko kokarin hawa jirgin da ke tafiya. Labari daga Wendy Smith, wadda ta rasa danta mai shekaru 15 mai suna Ricky sanadin hadarin jirgin, ya kara bayyana radadin irin waɗannan mummunan abubuwa. Network Rail na kira da a guje wa hanyoyin rikitarwa a tafarkin jirgin kasa, yana fadakar da mutane cewa hadarin ba zai taɓa kyau ba, kuma yana amfani da labarai na ainihi da shawarar kwararru don karfafawa.

article_content: Honor Blackman, recognized for her roles in 'Goldfinger' and 'The Avengers,' fondly shares her favorite travel stories. She loves taking quick trips to Paris and Amsterdam, mainly to explore their renowned art galleries. Her ideal getaway, though, is relaxing at a villa with a garden and pool, surrounded by her adult children and grandchildren. Spain ranks as her top destination, where she owns a small home and enjoys the warm sunshine. She remembers earlier days with her late second husband, Maurice Kaufman, when they used to sunbathe constantly—although now, she prefers staying in the shade. Some of her most unforgettable travels are linked to her acting work. She filmed 'Shalako' and 'The Man In The Moon' in Spain and spent eight months in Sydney with her children while performing in 'Move Over Mrs Markham.' During the making of 'Goldfinger,' she shot scenes in Kentucky, Miami, and Pinewood Studios with co-star Sean Connery. Looking forward, Honor hopes to visit New England one autumn to see the colorful leaves. She much prefers traveling with family, and recently celebrated her 89th birthday with a lovely trip to Sussex, organized by her son. While waiting at airports and on flights, she is currently busy writing her memories as a WWII evacuee for a future BBC television program. This year also marks the 50th anniversary of 'Goldfinger,' where she is remembered for playing Pussy Galore.

Amma abin da tafi so musamman shi ne hutu a villa mai lambu da tafkin waha, tare da manyan ’ya’yanta da jikokinta. A Spain ne tafi so sosai, inda take da ƙaramin gida kuma tana jin daɗin rana. Ta tuna lokacinta da marigayi mijinta na biyu, Maurice Kaufman, suna yawan yin rana—amma yanzu zama a inuwa yafi mata. Wasu daga cikin mafi shahararrun tafiye-tafiyenta suna da alaƙa da aikinta. Ta yi fim ɗin 'Shalako' da 'The Man In The Moon' a Spain, kuma ta shafe watanni takwas a Sydney tare da ’ya’yanta a lokacin da take wasa a 'Move Over Mrs Markham.' Lokacin 'Goldfinger,' an ɗauki hotuna a Kentucky, Miami da Pinewood Studios tare da Sean Connery. Honor na fatan ziyartar New England a lokacin kaka domin ganin ganyaye masu kala-kala. Tana matuƙar jin daɗin tafiya da iyalanta, kuma kwanan nan ta yi hutu ta musamman a Sussex domin murnar zagayowar ranar haihuwarta ta 89, wanda ɗanta ya ɗauke ta. A filin jirgin sama da cikin jirgi, tana amfani da lokacinta wajen rubuta tarihin rayuwarta a matsayin wacce aka kwashe lokacin Yakin Duniya na Biyu don wani shirin BBC. Bana an cika shekaru 50 da fitowar 'Goldfinger,' inda aka fi tunawa da ita a matsayin Pussy Galore.

article_content: Inflation remained elevated but unchanged in September, according to the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data released Thursday. CPI increased by 3.7% over the last 12 months, slightly above the forecasted 3.6%, and identical to August’s annual change. Month-over-month, prices grew by 0.4% from August to September—less than the previous month’s 0.6% increase, but still above the 0.3% prediction. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, also rose by 4.1% year-over-year, matching expectations, with a monthly uptick of 0.3%. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that shelter expenses made up over half of the monthly rise, with a 0.6% increase in September (up from 0.3% in August) and a 7.2% spike over the past year. Gasoline prices were another major factor, increasing 2.1% month-to-month in September—smaller than August's 10.6%, but higher than July’s 0.2%. Annually, gas prices rose by 3%. Food prices continued to climb as well, with a 0.2% monthly increase and a 3.7% annual uptick. After adjusting for inflation, real hourly earnings decreased by 0.2% from August to September since the 0.2% wage increase was outpaced by the 0.4% inflation rate. Meanwhile, job growth was robust, with the U.S. adding 336,000 nonfarm jobs in September, surpassing August's 227,000 gain. Julia Pollak, chief economist at ZipRecruiter, characterized the jobs report as ‘a best of all worlds’ scenario, suggesting that job growth isn't compromising inflation control. Additionally, Producer Price Index data released Wednesday showed a slowdown in price increases for final demand goods, possibly signaling gentler future consumer price hikes. Gregory Daco, chief economist at EY, pointed out that while supply chain improvements are lessening, lower service price growth could help hold down inflation in the months ahead.

Core CPI, wanda baya hada abinci da makamashi, shima ya karu da kashi 4.1% a shekara, ya yi daidai da tsammanin masana, sai kuma karin wata-wata na kashi 0.3%. A shekara guda, farashin fetur ya karu da kashi 3%. Farashin abinci ya ci gaba da hauhawa da karin wata-wata na kashi 0.2% da kuma karin shekara-shekara na kashi 3.7%. A lokaci guda, aikin neman aiki ya karu sosai inda aka samu karin ayyuka har 336,000 a fannin ba da aikin noma a Satumba, wanda ya zarce karin da aka samu a Agusta na 227,000. Gregory Daco, babbar masani a EY, ya ce duk da cewa saukin cunkoson hanyoyin samar da kaya ya ragu, raguwar hauhawar farashi a sabis na iya taimakawa rage hauhawar farashi nan gaba.

article_content: Buying gold during Indian festivals like Dhanteras, Diwali, and Akshaya Tritiya is a valued tradition, believed to bring luck. The price of gold jewellery varies by location, karat, and retailer, so researching prices beforehand is smart. In India, 22-karat gold (91.6% pure) is widely used for jewellery, while 18KT and 14KT pieces are also available at lower costs due to lesser gold content. On November 9, 2023, Tanishq sold 22KT gold at Rs 5,816 per gram, and Malabar, Joyallukas, and Kalyan Jewellers quoted Rs 5,570 per gram, as reported on their websites. The cost of gold jewellery depends on the gold’s purity, the alloys mixed in, and the making charges, which are higher for hand-made or intricate designs. Machine-made pieces generally cost less. The advertised rates exclude GST and making charges. Gold hallmarking, overseen by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), affirms gold purity. Since April 2023, all gold jewellery must have a unique six-digit HUID code, with sales prohibited otherwise. When purchasing, buyers should confirm the gold’s purity, be familiar with return policies and guarantees, and ensure the bill is detailed and transparent. Other news includes Tata Group’s $750 million acquisition of a Wistron facility, making it the first Indian iPhone assembler; India overtaking China in the QS Asian university rankings; and Religare’s independent directors accusing the Burman family of irregularities in a proposed takeover.

article_content: Emma Hayes, currently the only female manager in the Women's Super League (WSL) top flight, has expressed her ambition to coach in men’s professional football. Hayes led Chelsea to a second-place finish in the just-concluded WSL season, with Liverpool securing the title on goal difference. The 38-year-old, previously head coach of the Chicago Red Stars, has spent the last two years with Chelsea. She joined at a time when English women’s football was gaining stronger support from the Football Association and major clubs. A native Londoner, Hayes initially moved to the United States in search of professional prospects, as opportunities in England’s women’s football were limited. This situation is now improving. Notably, Shelley Kerr, once Arsenal Ladies manager, currently coaches the Stirling University men’s team in Scotland—a sign that doors are opening for women in football coaching, even in the men’s game. Hayes commented: 'All coaches aspire to reach the highest level possible, and I am no different. If my next opportunity was in the men’s game, I’d embrace it. Still, there should be more female coaches leading at the top of the women’s game before many move into men’s football.' A UEFA A Licence is a requirement for WSL managers, and Hayes urges those running the women’s game to have confidence in qualified female candidates. Liverpool manager Matt Beard and captain Gemma Bonner recently celebrated their WSL title win. Hayes addressed Kick It Out’s Women’s Raise Your Game conference at Upton Park, discussing growing opportunities in football for women, including in coaching, media, and sports science. She added, 'After ten years in America, I now have the chance to build a career at Chelsea, creating opportunities not only for players but also for staff. This is a truly significant time for women’s football nationwide.'

article_content: Climate change will cause irreversible damage to the Great Barrier Reef by 2030 unless immediate action is taken, marine scientists have warned. Australia's iconic natural heritage site is at a critical point, with coral projected to be destroyed for hundreds, if not thousands, of years due to rising carbon dioxide levels and global temperatures, according to a report published today. Experts are calling for greater commitment to reduce carbon emissions to help protect the reef, which has already lost about half of its coral coverage since the 1980s due to climate change, now its predominant threat. Scientists warn that the Great Barrier Reef will be irreversibly damaged by 2030 unless the average global temperature remains below the internationally agreed 2°C increase from pre-industrial levels. According to University of Queensland reef researcher Ove Hoegh-Guldberg, co-author of the 'Lights Out For the Reef' report, it is highly unlikely that coral reefs will survive beyond this threshold. Hoegh-Guldberg said that if current 'business as usual' trends continue, with global temperatures rising by 4°C, it would mean the end of the Great Barrier Reef. Even with the best-case 2°C scenario, most corals would still disappear. Without intervention, bacteria would overtake the dead coral, sand would dissolve, and the reef would lose its defining features. He cited coral bleaching—caused by excessively warm sea water temperatures and first recorded on the Reef in 1979—as a serious threat. Rising sea temperatures cause coral to bleach and die more quickly. Hoegh-Guldberg emphasized in the report’s foreword, compiled by WWF for Earth Hour, that urgent action is required to relieve both local and global stresses on the reef. 'This is not just speculation or alarmism by environmentalists. It is the conclusion of the world's most qualified coral reef experts,' he wrote. The Great Barrier Reef generates $6 billion annually in tourism revenue and supports 63,000 jobs. 'It is highly unlikely that coral reefs will survive an average global temperature increase of more than two degrees relative to pre-industrial levels,' Hoegh-Guldberg said. He added that if carbon pollution continues on its current path, the world is headed for at least three degrees of warming, which would cause irreversible harm to the reef by 2030. Co-author Dr Selina Ward told the Sydney Morning Herald that one of the reef's most important roles is serving as a wave barrier, protecting coastal islands from being swamped. The Great Barrier Reef—home to immense marine biodiversity—will be the focus of Australia's Earth Hour campaign, encouraging people and organizations to switch off their lights for one hour on March 29 in support of climate change awareness. The report comes as the reef, one of the world's most vulnerable ecosystems to climate change, faces the possibility of having its World Heritage status downgraded by UNESCO to 'world heritage in danger.' Despite these threats, Australia approved a major coal port expansion in the reef region in December, including dumping dredged waste within the marine park's boundaries—raising further environmental concerns.
translated_content: Masana kimiyyar teku sun gargadi cewa sauyin yanayi zai jawo mummunar illa da ba za a iya juyawa ba ga Reef ɗin Babban Gari na Australiya nan da 2030 idan ba a ɗauki mataki cikin gaggawa ba. Wurin tarihin kasa mai daraja na Australiya yana cikin mawuyacin hali, inda ake hasashen lalacewar koralai na ɗaruruwan ko dubban shekaru sakamakon ƙaruwa na carbon dioxide da zafin jikin duniya, in ji wani rahoto da aka fitar yau. Masana suna kiraye-kiraye da a ƙara ƙoƙari wajen rage fitar da hayakin carbon don kare reef ɗin, wanda tuni ya rasa kusan rabin koralinsa tun shekarun 1980 saboda sauyin yanayi, yanzu shine babban barazana gare shi. Masana sun gargadi cewa Reef ɗin Babban Gari zai lalace matuƙa, ba za a iya dawo da shi ba, zuwa 2030 idan zafin jikin duniya bai tsaya ƙasa da ƙaruwa ta 2°C da aka amince da ita a kasashen duniya kafin masana’antu ba. A cewar masanin reef daga Jami’ar Queensland, Ove Hoegh-Guldberg, wanda ya rubuta rahoton 'Lights Out For the Reef', ba a sa ran reef zai iya rayuwa bayan wannan ƙimar ba. Hoegh-Guldberg ya ce, idan lamura suka cigaba kamar yanzu kuma zafin jikin duniya ya ƙaru da 4°C, hakan zai zama ƙarshen Reef ɗin Babban Gari. Ko a mafi kyawun yanayi na 2°C, yawancin koralai za su shuɗe. Idan ba a ɗauki mataki ba, bacteria za su mamaye matattun koralai, yashi ya narke, reef ɗin kuma zai rasa muhimmancinsa. Ya bayyana cewa bleaching na koralai—sakamakon zafin ruwan teku da ya fi kima kuma aka fara lura da shi tun 1979 a reef ɗin—babbar barazana ce. Karin zafin ruwan teku na sa koralai yin bleaching da mutuwa cikin gaggawa. Hoegh-Guldberg ya jaddada a gabatarwar rahoton, wanda WWF ta hada don Earth Hour, cewa wajibi ne a dauki mataki cikin gaggawa don rage matsin lamba daga gida da waje akan reef ɗin. Ya ce, 'Wannan ba kawai zato ko fargabar masu kishin muhalli ba ne. Wannan hukunci ne daga kwararru a fannin reef na duniya.' Reef ɗin Babban Gari na samar da dala biliyan 6 a shekara daga yawon bude ido, yana kuma samar da ayyuka 63,000. Hoegh-Guldberg ya ce 'Ba za a iya sa ran reef ɗin ya tsira ba idan zafin jikin duniya ya zarce digiri biyu tun kafin masana’antu.' Ya kuma kara da cewa idanu aka ci gaba da fitar da hayakin carbon kamar yanzu, duniya tana kan hanyarsa ta kai digiri uku, wanda zai jawo mummunar illa ga reef kafin 2030. Dr Selina Ward, wata marubuciyar rahoton, ta shaida wa Sydney Morning Herald cewa daya daga cikin manyan ayyukan reef ɗin shine zama kariya ga tsibirai daga ambaliyar ruwa. Reef ɗin Babban Gari—muhalli mai yawan nau'o'in halittu a karkashin ruwa—zai kasance a jigon kamfen din Earth Hour na Australiya, yana karfafa mutane da kungiyoyi su kashe fitilu na tsawon awa daya a ranar 29 ga Maris don wayar da kai game da sauyin yanayi. Rahoton ya fito ne a kan lokaci, yayin da reef ɗin, daya daga cikin wuraren da ke cikin matukar hadari ga sauyin yanayi, ke fuskantar yiyuwar rage martaba ta 'world heritage' na UNESCO zuwa 'world heritage in danger'. Duk da wadannan barazana, Australiya ta amince da fadada tashar kwal a yankin reef a watan Disamba, ciki har da zubar da kura daga banbarewa cikin filin kiyayewa na teku—abinda ke kara damuwar muhalli.

article_content: Aspiritech is a nonprofit organization based in Highland Park, Illinois, that employs adults with autism as software testers. The company recognizes that traits commonly associated with autism—such as attention to detail, strong focus, and comfort with repetitive tasks—make individuals particularly well-suited for software testing roles. The organization was founded by Moshe and Brenda Weitzberg after their son Oran, who was diagnosed with Asperger’s syndrome at age 14, struggled to keep a job bagging groceries. Oran now works at Aspiritech, where his abilities have helped him become one of their top software testers. Aspiritech’s supportive work environment accommodates differences that often make employment challenging for adults with autism, such as social awkwardness and sensitivity to sensory input. Clients, including companies like HandHold Adaptive and ISI Telemanagement Solutions, have been pleased with Aspiritech’s work, describing the employees as detail-oriented and quick to learn. The company’s name blends 'Asperger’s,' 'spirit,' and 'technology.' Aspiritech’s approach is based on the Danish company Specialisterne, which also hires people with autism as software testers. Aspiritech projects earning $120,000 this year, with about 60 percent from donations and 40 percent from clients, aiming to increase client revenue in the coming year. Industry experts note that adults with autism often face high unemployment rates, though exact numbers are unknown. Research and support services have mostly focused on children, leaving many adults with autism without resources or employment opportunities. By providing meaningful job experiences, Aspiritech is helping fill this gap. Employees earn $12 to $15 an hour and work in an environment that respects their individual needs. The company also organizes social activities like bowling and miniature golf to help staff build social skills. While some employees hope to advance into other technology roles, working at Aspiritech provides valuable job skills and experience for their futures.

article_content: A couple and their teenage son tragically died while attempting to save their dog from the ocean, as their daughter and the son's girlfriend watched from the shore. Mary Elena Scott, 57, and Howard Gregory Kuljian, 54, drowned on Saturday afternoon at Big Lagoon, a beach near Eureka, around 300 miles north of San Francisco, California. Authorities have called off the search for their son, Gregory James Kuljian, who remains missing and is presumed dead. The family’s dog managed to climb out of the water on its own. The incident began when powerful 10-foot waves pulled the dog into the sea as it chased a thrown stick. Gregory, known as 'Geddie' to friends, rushed in to rescue the dog. Witnessing his son, Mr. Kuljian followed him. Although the teenager briefly made it out, he and his mother went back into the water to search for his father, and both were swept away. The couple’s daughter, 18-year-old Olivia, and Gregory’s girlfriend could only watch helplessly from the beach. A bystander called 911 at 12:40 p.m. to report the emergency, but rescuers could not reach the family in time. A park ranger ran half a mile to get to the scene but was unable to enter the water due to the high surf. Ms. Scott’s body was recovered from the ocean, while Mr. Kuljian’s body washed ashore. The Coast Guard used a helicopter and two motor life boats to search for the missing teenager, but suspended the aerial search by 7 p.m. Saturday due to thick fog. The search continued Sunday with no further discoveries. By Monday, officials called off the search, although the Sheriff’s department continues occasional checks along the coast. According to Coast Guard Lt. Bernie Garrigan, surviving in the cold water without a wetsuit would have been unlikely. Warning signs about dangerous 'sneaker waves' are posted near the beach, as these waves can unexpectedly surge up the shore and pull people out to sea. Community members memorialized the family on social media, organizing a 'Wear Green for Geddie' event in remembrance. Ian Johnson, who started the page, described Geddie as friendly, humorous, and well-liked. The family lived in Freshwater, Eureka, California. Records show Howard Kuljian was a graduate student and teacher at the Department of Forestry at Humboldt State University in 2010.

article_content: Afghanistan is on the verge of reaching the World Cup semifinals and will meet Australia for a rare contest, as Australia has previously canceled bilateral matches in protest against the Taliban’s policies restricting women’s participation in sports. Coach Jonathan Trott has encouraged Afghanistan’s players to challenge expectations in India by emphasizing that they are there to compete and win. This mindset has underpinned Afghanistan’s tournament performance, helping them recover from early defeats to Bangladesh and India, and claim victories over England, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and the Netherlands. The team now prepares for a high-stakes game against Australia in Mumbai. Trott admits Australia remains the favorite, noting Afghanistan’s underdog status due to less success in bilateral series. However, Trott points to his team’s increased confidence after beating former World Cup champions and questions why defeating Australia isn't possible as well. However, this match occurs against a backdrop of wider controversy. Cricket Australia has twice canceled bilateral series with Afghanistan over two years, reacting to Afghanistan’s diminishing women’s rights under Taliban rule. CA made these decisions with input from the Australian government and Afghan women cricketers seeking refuge in Australia. Nonetheless, CA continues to participate against Afghanistan in ICC-tournament matches, as these are governed by ICC protocols. The Afghanistan Cricket Board, which achieved full ICC membership in 2017 alongside Ireland, faces scrutiny regarding gender equality. At the time of joining, the ACB committed (without specific deadlines) to developing women’s cricket, but these plans halted when the Taliban barred women from playing sports after taking power in 2021. The ICC asserts ongoing support for the ACB in developing cricket within Afghanistan’s legal framework, stopping short of imposing sanctions or stricter requirements, even as Ireland operates both men’s and women’s teams. While cricket has grown in Afghanistan—mainly through returning refugees—the discontinuation of women’s cricket is at odds with the ICC’s push for women’s participation globally. Some advocate funding restrictions or earmarking support for women’s programs, but a total suspension of Afghanistan from international cricket appears unlikely. Afghanistan’s rapid cricket progress is unique, as the nation embraced the sport without a colonial past. Its journey is significant at a time when cricket is expanding its reach, with moves towards Olympic inclusion and T20 leagues in places like the US. When asked about the broader controversy, Trott avoids political commentary, highlighting instead his players’ positive demeanor and the international support for Afghanistan’s team. He emphasizes their representation of both cricket and their country, noting their uplifting impact in Afghanistan and abroad, even as debates over equality persist.

article_content: Dr. Laura Tafe, a pathologist at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center, created a collage titled 'Compassion' that appears in the book 'Artists Remaking Medicine.' She says this artwork expresses her vision for a healthcare system where empathy and compassion flow freely between patients and medical staff. In 2016, Emily Peters became a statistic in the maternal health crisis after a rare complication called an amniotic fluid embolism left her in intensive care. During her stay, she encountered several problems, such as being separated from her healthy newborn unless she and her husband paid for private nursing care. Motivated by these experiences, Peters sought out ways to fix the system’s flaws—one solution being the use of art to help reimagine medicine. Peters believes healthcare’s lack of creativity keeps people locked into a dehumanizing status quo, and that artists can help envision a more compassionate future. Her book 'Artists Remaking Medicine' brings together artists, musicians, writers, physicians, and public health professionals to explore how creativity can make healthcare more humane. Rather than policy prescriptions, the book offers stories and projects to inspire a much-needed cultural shift. Examples include electronic musician Yoko Sen, who redesigned ICU alarms to create gentler sounds for patients, and the collective MSCHF, who turned stacks of medical bills into art, raising over $73,000 to pay off patients’ debts. Similarly, an art event in Philadelphia involved burning a giant medical bill effigy and collected enough funding to cancel $1.6 million in medical debt. Peters argues that art makes activism vivid, keeping issues like rising medical costs at the forefront. The book highlights creative mediums like puppetry, color theory, and music as a way to spark deeper conversations about systemic change. For instance, photographer Kathleen Sheffer used her camera post–heart-lung transplant to assert her personhood in a hospital environment. Dr. Stella Sapho, a New York physician featured in the book, discusses how many healthcare professionals feel powerless, pointing to a ‘crisis of imagination’ in medicine. Peters says artists are adept at engaging with complexity and imagining alternatives. Peters’s own traumatic hospital experience revealed many system weaknesses, from confusing layouts to dismissed requests for a different nurse. She reflects on traditions like the white coat ceremony and the choice of ‘medical green’—both relatively modern inventions—showing that many things about medicine can be rethought. A survey she ran for the book found patients wanted bright, unconventional colors in hospitals, challenging assumptions about what makes a healing environment. Projects such as the MASS Design Group’s Butaro District Hospital in Rwanda demonstrate how local collaboration, sustainable design, and open spaces can foster healing for both patients and communities. The hospital features gardens, open-air corridors, and natural light to connect people with one another and the environment. Though some criticize incorporating art into healthcare as unnecessary or costly, Peters insists it’s a vital response to real financial and human crises. The book’s exploration of puppetry, for example, shows how creative techniques can help medical trainees develop empathy and present themselves more authentically. Peters concludes that embracing creativity and even humor can reduce burnout and help reconnect practitioners with their sense of mission, making healthcare a more human experience for everyone.

Ta bayyana cewa wannan aikin zane yana nuna burinta na ganin tsarin lafiyan da tausayi da jin kai ke gudana tsakanin marasa lafiya da ma'aikatan lafiya. A shekarar 2016, Emily Peters ta shiga cikin matsalar mutuwar uwa bayan haihuwa bayan wani mummunan hadari mai suna amniotic fluid embolism ya jefa ta a dakin kulawa na gaggawa. A lokacin zamanta a asibiti, ta fuskanci matsaloli da dama kamar raba ta da jaririnta kafin ta biya kudin bayar da kulawa na musamman. Littafin ba ya mai da hankali ga dokoki kawai, sai dai labarai da ayyuka na musamman don tayar da sabon salo. A cikin littafin an kawo misalin mawaki Yoko Sen, wacce ta sake kirkiro sautin kayan aikin ICU don su rika yin laushi a kunnen marasa lafiya, da kuma kungiyar MSCHF, wacce ta yi amfani da takardun biyan kudin asibiti wajen yin zane-zane sannan ta tara sama da $73,000 don biya wa marasa lafiya basussukan su. Hakazalika, an gudanar da wani taron fasaha a Philadelphia inda aka kone babban katin biyan kudin asibiti sannan aka tara kudin da ya kai har an biya bashin $1.6 miliyan na wasu marasa lafiya. Peters ta ce, fasaha na sa mutane su ci gaba da himma wajen yaki da matsalolin kudi a kiwon lafiya. Littafin ya nuna abubuwa irin su kwaikwayo da launuka da waka don farfado da muhawara mai zurfi game da gyaran fannin. A wani labari a littafin, Kathleen Sheffer, mai daukar hoto, ta yi amfani da kamara bayan dashen zuciya da huhu don tabbatar da mutuncinta a asibiti. Dr. Stella Sapho, wata likita a New York, ta bayyana yadda mafi yawan ma'aikatan lafiya ke jin rashin iko, tana kiran hakan 'crisis of imagination.' Peters ta ce masu fasaha sun fi kowa iya fuskantar matsaloli masu rikitarwa da kawo sabon mafita. Kwarewar Peters kanta tana cikin asibiti ta bankado matsaloli da dama – daga rikici a tsarin asibiti har zuwa rashin amsa korafinta. Ta tuno yadda wasu al'adu irin su bikin sa riga fari dana 'medical green' duka sabbin abubuwa ne da za a iya duba su. A wata amsa tambaya da tayi a littafin, mutane sun nuna suna sha’awar launuka masu ban sha'awa a asibiti, sabanin abin da ake gani a yanzu. Ayyukan MASS Design Group na asibitin Butaro a Rwanda sun nuna yadda hadin gwiwar cikin gida, da amfani da kayan gida da shimfidar waje ke kawo waraka ga al'umma da marasa lafiya. Asibitin na da lambuna, hanyoyi masu budewa da hasken rana yana shigowa don hada mutane da juna da muhallinsu. Ko da yake wasu na ganin shigo da fasaha cikin kiwon lafiya tamkar kashe kudi ne, Peters ta dage cewa wajibi ne a dauka a matsayin mafita ga matsalolin kudi da na jin kai. Littafin ya bayar da misalai kamar kwaikwayo don koyar da matasa likitoci yin tausayi da nuna gaskiya ga marasa lafiya. A karshe, Peters na fatan kirkira da dariya su rage gajiya a tsakanin ma'aikatan lafiya kuma su dawo da alakar dan Adam da dacewa a fannin kiwon lafiya.

article_content: A British tribunal recently decided that the U.K.'s privacy regulator, the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), has no authority to enforce penalties against Clearview AI. Clearview AI is an American company known for collecting billions of facial images—including those of U.K. citizens—without their consent. Last year, the ICO fined Clearview over £7.5 million ($9.1 million) and ordered it to delete U.K. residents' data after ruling that the company breached General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) by not informing people or getting their approval. Information commissioner John Edwards criticized Clearview's business for monitoring people and turning their behavior into a marketable service. Clearview appealed, and now a judge has agreed with the company, ruling that its gathering and processing of data were linked to law enforcement services outside the U.K., so British privacy laws don't apply. Clearview's technology has previously been tested in the U.K. by the Metropolitan Police, Ministry of Defence, and National Crime Agency. Today, its clients are mainly law enforcement and national security bodies in countries like the U.S., Panama, Brazil, Mexico, Dominican Republic, and Ukraine. In 2020, after settling a lawsuit with the American Civil Liberties Union in Illinois, Clearview restricted its services to government agencies and related contractors. With this court ruling, the ICO cannot regulate the actions of foreign governments using Clearview’s tools. The ICO says it's reviewing the decision and will consider its next steps, emphasizing that this only covers foreign law enforcement agencies and doesn't prevent action against international businesses that misuse U.K. residents' data otherwise. Clearview AI has faced similar legal issues worldwide, for example in France, Italy, and Greece, where authorities found it violated GDPR—though it hasn't always paid fines or proven data deletion. Canada and Australia have also acted against the company. After the latest U.K. decision, Clearview’s general counsel Jack Mulcaire said the company is satisfied with the judgment.

Wannan kamfani yana tattara dubban biliyoyin hotunan fuskokin mutane, har da 'yan Birtaniya, ba tare da izininsu ba. A bara, ICO ta ci tarar Clearview AI fiye da fam miliyan 7.5 ($9.1 miliyan) tare da umartar kamfanin ya goge bayanan 'yan ƙasar, bayan an tabbatar da karya dokar kare bayanai ta GDPR saboda rashin sanar da jama'a ko neman yardarsu. Shugaban ICO, John Edwards, ya zargi kasuwancin Clearview da leƙen ɗan Adam da kuma sayar da bayanan halayyar mutane a matsayin sabis. Clearview AI ta ɗaukaka ƙara, kuma yanzu alkali ya amince da kamfanin, inda ya yanke hukunci cewa ayyukan tattara bayanai na Clearview sun shafi hukumomin 'yan sanda na ƙasashen waje ne, don haka dokokin kare bayanai na Birtaniya ba su shafi lamarin ba. An gwada fasahar Clearview a sashen 'yan sanda, Ma'aikatar Tsaro, da hukumar yaƙi da manyan laifuka a Birtaniya. A yanzu, yawancin abokan cinikin sa su ne hukumomin tsaro da 'yan sanda a ƙasashen Amurka, Panama, Brazil, Mexico, Dominican Republic, da Ukraine. A shekarar 2020, bayan sasanci da ƙungiyar ACLU a Illinois, Clearview ta takaita ayyukanta ga hukumomin gwamnati da masu aiki da su. Saboda wannan hukunci, ICO ba za ta iya sa ido kan yadda gwamnatocin ƙasashen waje ke amfani da fasahar Clearview ba. ICO ta bayyana cewa tana nazarin hukuncin kuma za ta duba matakin da ya dace, tana mai jaddada cewa wannan hukuncin na shafi hukumomin tsaron ƙasashen waje ne kawai, ba ya hana ICO daukar mataki kan kamfanoni na ƙetare da ke amfani da bayanan 'yan ƙasar ba bisa ƙa'ida ba. Clearview AI ta fuskanci kalubale makamancin haka a ƙasashe irinsu Faransa, Italiya da Girka, inda aka same ta da laifin karya dokar GDPR—duk da cewa ba a tabbatar da biyan tarar ko gogewar bayanai ba har yanzu. Kanada da Ostiraliya ma sun dauki mataki kan kamfanin. Bayan sabuwar hukunci a Birtaniya, lauya na Clearview AI, Jack Mulcaire, ya bayyana jin daɗin su game da wannan hukunci.

article_content: Iranian officials plan to prevent women from attending live broadcasts of soccer matches in public cinemas, as reported by ILNA. The proposed restriction comes after a business oversight police agency argued that the presence of women and families could cause security issues and inappropriate actions in theaters. Cinemas in Iran's main cities have been screening Asian Cup matches, where Iran's team has advanced to the quarterfinals. Amir Hossein Alamalhoda, a representative of the cinema industry, said the Ministry of Culture and Guidance will make the final decision. Women are already not allowed at men's soccer games in stadiums—a policy conservative religious and government figures support, saying it aligns with Islamic principles. Journalist Farbod Jamali also contributed to this news.

article_content: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Wednesday declared null and void the Pakistan government's notification authorizing a jail trial for former Prime Minister Imran Khan in the cipher case, where he faces charges of leaking state secrets. A two-member bench delivered its reserved judgment on an intra-court appeal filed by Khan, overturning an earlier single-bench decision that had rejected his plea against being tried in Adiala Jail, Rawalpindi. Khan, age 71, has been held at Adiala Jail since September 26, after being transferred from District Jail, Attock. The Ministry of Law had issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the jail trial on August 29, following requests from the Interior Ministry and special court Judge Abual Hasnat Zulqarnain. Earlier on Wednesday, Justices Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb and Saman Rafat Imtiaz heard Khan's intra-court appeal, reserving judgment after concluding arguments. According to the short verdict, the government's notification dated August 29 authorizing the jail trial was declared illegal. However, the court clarified that a jail trial is not prohibited in extraordinary circumstances, provided there is judicial oversight and a formal ruling by the trial judge, followed by a government notification. The IHC accepted the intra-court appeal against its single-bench verdict from October 16 and declined to grant retrospective effect to a Cabinet decision from November 15 that approved the jail trial. The court also upheld the appointment of Judge Abual Hasnat Zulqarnain, who is overseeing Khan's trial under the Official Secrets Act. Uncertainty persists regarding the validity of proceedings already conducted in jail, as the court's ruling was based on procedural and technical grounds. Senior lawyer Yasin Azad told Samaa TV that the jail trial has been halted, but the government can address procedural gaps or appeal to the Supreme Court. He added that Khan's indictment remains intact. In contrast, lawyer Abid Zuberi argued that by rejecting the jail trial, the court has nullified all associated proceedings and actions. Former Advocate General Jehangir Jadoon stated that the court based its decision on procedural flaws, and more clarity would follow in the detailed judgment. In March 2022, Imran Khan and then-Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi were alleged to have violated secrecy laws by mishandling a diplomatic cable sent by Pakistan's embassy in Washington, which then went missing. Both men, who claimed the cable contained a US threat to oust the PTI government, were indicted on October 23. Their formal trial began recently with witness statements being recorded. The IHC had previously upheld the indictment when challenged by Khan but stayed the trial pending a ruling on the intra-court appeal.
translated_content: Babban Kotun Birnin Islamabad (IHC) a ranar Laraba ta soke sanarwar gwamnatin Pakistan da ta amince da shari’ar tsohon Firaminista Imran Khan a gidan yari a shari’ar cipher, inda ake zarginsa da fitar da sirrin kasa. Kwamitin alkalan biyu ne ya zartar da wannan hukunci bayan sauraron karar Imran Khan, inda suka rushe hukuncin alkali daya da bai amince da bukatar Khan na a daina shari’a a gidan yarin Adiala da ke Rawalpindi ba. Imran Khan mai shekaru 71 yana tsare a gidan yarin Adiala tun 26 ga Satumba, bayan an kawo shi daga gidan yarin Attock. Ma’aikatar Shari’a ta fitar da NOC na shari’ar gidan yari a ranar 29 ga Agusta, bayan bukatar Ma’aikatar Harkokin Cikin Gida da alkalin kotu ta musamman Abual Hasnat Zulqarnain. Da safiyar Laraba, alkalan Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb da Saman Rafat Imtiaz sun saurari karar Khan, suka adana hukunci bayan kammala shari’ar. A hukunci, an bayyana sanarwar gwamnatin ta 29 ga Agusta da ta amince da shari’a a gidan yari da babu inganci. Sai dai, kotu ta fayyace cewa shari’a a gidan yari ba a haramta ta gaba daya ba idan akwai dalilai na musamman, muddin alkali ya bada umarni kuma gwamnati ta fitar da sanarwa. IHC ta amince da daukaka karar kan hukuncin da alkali daya ya yanke a ranar 16 ga Oktoba, amma ta ki amincewa da yunkurin Majalisar Ministoci na 15 ga Nuwamba da ya amince da shari’ar gidan yari. Haka kuma, kotun ta tabbatar da nadin alkalin Abual Hasnat Zulqarnain da ke jagorantar shari’ar a karkashin Dokar Sirrin Gwamnati. Har yanzu akwai shakku kan halaccin shari’ar da aka fara a gidan yari, ganin cewa hukuncin kotun ya danganci dokoki da tsarin aiki. Lauya Yasin Azad ya bayyana wa Samaa TV cewa an dakatar da shari’ar gidan yari a yanzu, amma gwamnati na iya gyara matsalolin tsarin ko ta daukaka kara zuwa Kotun Koli. Ya kara da cewa tuhumar da aka yi wa Khan tana nan. A nasu bangare, lauya Abid Zuberi yace kotun ta soke duk wani mataki da aka dauka kan shari’ar gidan yari. Tsohon Babban Lauya Jehangir Jadoon ya ce kotu ta rushe tsarin tsarin da gwamnati ta bi, kuma karin bayani zai fito a cikakken hukunci. A watan Maris na 2022 ne ake zargin Imran Khan da tsohon Ministan Harkokin Waje Shah Mahmood Qureshi da karya dokar asiri wajen tafiyar da wata wasikar diflomasiyya daga ofishin jakadancin Pakistan da ke Washington, wadda daga bisani ta bace. Su biyun sun ce wasikar na dauke da barazanar Amurka ta hambarar da gwamnatin PTI, kuma an tuhume su a ranar 23 ga Oktoba. An fara shari’ar kwanan nan, inda aka fara karbar shaida. IHC ta tabbatar da tuhumar da aka yi wa Khan lokacin da aka daukaka kara, amma ta dakatar da shari’ar har zuwa yanke hukunci kan daukaka karar.

article_content:
Months after leaving the White House, former President Donald Trump allegedly discussed potentially sensitive U.S. nuclear submarine information with Anthony Pratt, an Australian billionaire and member of Trump's Mar-a-Lago Club. Pratt reportedly went on to share these details with more than 45 individuals, including over a dozen foreign officials, his own employees, and several journalists, according to sources familiar with the situation.

The alleged disclosure became part of Special Counsel Jack Smith's investigation into whether Trump mishandled classified documents at Mar-a-Lago. Prosecutors and FBI agents interviewed Pratt on at least two occasions this year. 

During interviews, Pratt described seeking to make conversation with Trump at Mar-a-Lago in April 2021 by mentioning the U.S. submarine fleet—a topic the two had previously discussed. According to Pratt’s account, Trump, eager and leaning toward Pratt in what appeared to be a discreet manner, shared two pieces of information: the supposed number of nuclear warheads carried on U.S. submarines and how close those submarines could reportedly approach Russian subs without being detected.

After the meeting, Pratt shared what Trump allegedly told him with at least 45 people, including six journalists, 11 of his employees, 10 Australian officials, and three former Australian prime ministers. Pratt clarified to investigators that he could not determine whether Trump's information was factual or just exaggeration, but investigators nevertheless asked him not to repeat the figures, suggesting the information could be sensitive.

A former Mar-a-Lago employee told investigators he overheard Pratt immediately recounting part of the conversation and expressed being "bothered" and "shocked" by Trump's sharing of seemingly sensitive information with a non-U.S. citizen. Pratt also told investigators that Trump never showed him any government documents during their meetings.

The disclosure coincided with ongoing negotiations between Australia and the Biden administration about the purchase of nuclear-powered submarines—a deal eventually completed, with Australia agreeing to buy at least three Virginia-class submarines, none of which will be equipped with nuclear weapons according to President Joe Biden.

Special Counsel Smith’s indictment against Trump did not mention the 2021 conversation with Pratt, though Trump faces 40 charges relating to the retention of national defense information and obstruction.

Pratt joined Mar-a-Lago after Trump became president in 2017 and has had several interactions with him, even pledging $2 billion in investment in U.S. manufacturing. Although Pratt was previously a vocal supporter of Trump, he recently told investigators that he now supports the current U.S. government, describing himself as someone who tends to "side with the king."

A Trump spokesperson dismissed the reporting as contextually lacking and reiterated that Trump acted properly and lawfully.

Majiyoyi sun ce Pratt ya yada wannan labari ga fiye da mutane 45, ciki har da jami’an kasashen waje, ma’aikatansa, da wasu 'yan jarida.

Wannan batu yana daga cikin abubuwan da lauya na musamman Jack Smith ke bincikawa kan yadda Trump ya mu’amala da takardun sirri a Mar-a-Lago. Masu bincike sun yi wa Pratt tambayoyi akalla sau biyu bana.

Pratt ya shiga Mar-a-Lago tun bayan Trump ya zama shugaban kasa, kuma ya sha mu'amala da shi, har ma ya alkawarta zuba jarin dala biliyan biyu a Amurka. Ko da a baya Pratt yana goyon bayan Trump, yanzu ya fada wa masu bincike cewa yana goyon bayan gwamnati mai ci.

Mai magana da yawun Trump ya ce labaran sun rasa mahallin su da cikakken bayani, yana kare cewa Trump bai yi laifi ba kuma ya bi doka yadda ya kamata.

article_content: Democrat Gabe Amo has won Rhode Island’s 1st Congressional District seat, making history as the state’s first Black member of Congress. Amo is the son of immigrants from Ghana and Liberia and formerly served as a White House aide. He succeeds Democrat David Cicilline, who resigned this summer to lead the Rhode Island Foundation. Upon his victory, Amo expressed gratitude for the chance to serve his district and the state. He said, “I’m humbled by the momentous opportunity to serve as the first person of color, but I didn’t run to make history.” At 35, Amo sees himself as one in a long line of advocates for civil rights and the working class. Amo pointed out the importance of Rhode Island’s immigrant stories and aims to ensure the federal government functions effectively. Other priorities include reducing gun violence and protecting Social Security and Medicare. He pledged to restore trust and confidence in government, despite what he described as chaos within the Republican Party. Amo, who grew up in Pawtucket, won a crowded Democratic primary with over 32% of the vote. He held positions in the Obama and Biden administrations, including as deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs, and served under former Governor Gina Raimondo. Amo attended Wheaton College and studied public policy at Oxford University, crediting his parents’ determination for his achievements. His mother was a nurse and his father opened a liquor store. After his primary win, Amo emphasized Rhode Island’s tradition of welcoming immigrants. During the campaign, he received the endorsement of former Congressman Patrick Kennedy. Amo supports restoring nationwide abortion rights, supports action on climate change, and advocates for stricter gun laws—including banning assault-style weapons, increasing CDC gun violence research, and implementing universal background checks. His election represents a continued shift from Rhode Island’s traditional Italian American political structure, previously led by the late Mayor Vincent ‘Buddy’ Cianci. Amo himself called it a generational change. Amo defeated Republican Gerry Leonard, a Marine veteran who won the GOP primary. Leonard graciously conceded, commended Amo's campaign, and said he hoped Amo would be a great congressman. Leonard had criticized President Biden’s economic policies while supporting U.S. aid to Ukraine. The last Republican to represent the district was Ron Machtley, who served from 1989 to 1995.

article_content: Heartwarming new photographs capture the gentle maternal side of Mary, a 27-year-old gorilla at Busch Gardens in Tampa, Florida. Mary gave birth to a baby girl on February 6 at 8:30 p.m. The images show Mary breastfeeding her week-old infant and admiring her lovingly. A video also highlights Mary protectively carrying her baby, who clings to the fur on Mary's stomach. According to Jeff Andrews, vice president of zoological operations at Busch Gardens, the first month will be crucial for Mary and her infant as they adjust to the existing gorilla troop. The animal care team will monitor their progress closely to ensure a smooth integration. Gorilla mothers devote considerable attention to their newborns, which typically weigh just four pounds at birth. The babies cling to their mothers to stay warm and begin riding on their mothers’ backs from the age of four months, continuing for nearly three years as they grow. This newborn, the third successful gorilla birth at Busch Gardens, has not yet been named. Bolingo, the suspected father, was the first gorilla born at the park in 2005. Mary arrived at Busch Gardens from Gladys Porter Zoo, Brownsville, Texas, in 2010, accompanied by her first daughter, Pele. Pele herself gave birth to Enzi just last December. The gorilla troop at the park now numbers seven. Visitors will soon have the chance to see the growing gorilla family in the Myombe Reserve habitat. The addition of the new baby gorilla is part of Busch Gardens’ involvement in the Association of Zoos and Aquariums’ Species Survival Plan (SSP), which seeks to protect and sustainably manage endangered species populations such as the lowland gorilla. According to the World Wildlife Fund, the population of Western lowland gorillas has declined by more than 60 percent in the past 20 to 25 years, leaving them critically endangered. In addition to threats from illegal hunting and deforestation, Western lowland gorillas have slow reproductive rates, as females do not reach sexual maturity until eight or nine years old and care for dependent young for up to five years.
translated_content: Hoton sabbin hoto masu tausayi sun nuna yadda Mary, guwarila mai shekaru 27 dake Busch Gardens a Tampa, Florida, ke kula da jaririyarta cikin kauna. Mary ta haifi yarinya a ranar 6 ga Fabrairu da karfe 8:30 na dare. Hotunan sun nuna Mary tana shayar da jaririyar mako guda sannan tana kallonta cikin sha’awa. A cikin wani bidiyo ma an ga yadda Mary ke rike da jaririyarta tana rungumeta, tana manne da fur a cikinta. A cewar Jeff Andrews, mataimakin shugaban ayyukan dabbobi a Busch Gardens, watan farko zai zama mai matukar muhimmanci ga Mary da jaririyarta yayin da za su sabawa sauran guwariloli a cikin rukunin. Tawagar masu kula da dabbobi za su sa ido matuka don tabbatar da samun saukin sabawa. Uwar guwarila kan mayar da hankali sosai wajen kula da jaririnta, wanda yawanci nauyinsa ba ya wuce fam hudu a haihuwa. Jariran na manne da mahaifiyarsu don jin zafi kuma daga watanni hudu suna fara hawa bayan uwar su, suna ci gaba da hakan har kusan shekaru uku suna girma. Jaririya wacce aka haifa yanzu haka ba a saka mata suna ba, ita ce karo na uku da aka samu nasarar haihuwar guwarila a Busch Gardens. Bolingo, da ake tsammanin shi ne uba, shi ne guwarila na farko da aka haifa a gonar a 2005. Mary ta iso Busch Gardens daga Gladys Porter Zoo, Brownsville, Texas a 2010 tare da ’yarta ta farko, Pele. Ita ma Pele ta haifi Enzi a watan Disamba da ya gabata. Jimillar guwarilan da ke gonar yanzu sun kai bakwai. Ba da jimawa ba baƙi za su sami damar ganin wannan ƙungiyar guwarilan na Myombe Reserve. Ƙarin wannan jariri na cikin shirin kare nau’in dabba (SSP) na haɗin gwiwa da Busch Gardens ke yi tare da Kungiyar lambunan dabbobi da gidan zoo na Amurka (AZA), domin kare da kiyayewa irinsu guwarilan lowland. Bayan barazanar farauta da sare gandun daji, guwarila mata na Western lowland ba sa haihuwa da yawa, domin sun fara girma ne bayan shekara takwas ko tara kuma suna jima suna kula da jariru har zuwa shekara biyar.

article_content: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the world's largest particle accelerator, is operational again after being idle for over a year because of an electrical malfunction. CERN, the European research body, celebrated the restart, with accelerator director Steve Myers describing the repair process as a massive effort. CERN confirmed that a circulating proton beam was established in the LHC's 17-mile tunnel on Friday, which is an essential milestone before scientific experimentation can fully commence. While it’s not quite ready for major experiments, this step advances researchers closer to starting physics research. Located underground at the border of Switzerland and France, the LHC has been gradually moving back toward activity. It achieved the necessary cold operating temperature in early October, with particle injections beginning soon after. Preliminary low-energy collision tests are anticipated within a week. Larger-scale high-energy experiments, important for significant physics discoveries, are slated for the following year. The LHC has faced technical hiccups as well—one incident involved a bird dropping bread into the machinery, resulting in a temporary halt. However, CERN notes such accidents didn’t cause major harm to the accelerator. After its celebrated first beam cycle in September 2008, the LHC suffered a significant setback when a defective connector among the thousands used in the magnet system caused substantial damage, requiring lengthy repairs. Experts like Mark Wise from Caltech remain enthusiastic, interpreting these obstacles as only minor setbacks common for equipment of such complexity. He’s confident that ongoing issues will be resolved and that progress will continue. CERN projects the LHC will run for at least two decades and holds hope that in just a few years, it might uncover breakthroughs such as the theoretical Higgs boson or hints of supersymmetry. The collider’s key experiments—ATLAS, CMS, and ALICE—aim to detect previously unobserved particles and mimic the universe’s earliest conditions, like the high-temperature quark-gluon plasma present just after the Big Bang. According to Yale’s John Harris, these studies will delve into new territory, investigating fundamental particles and energies that shaped the cosmos.
translated_content: Babban injin hanzarta zarra (LHC), wato Large Hadron Collider, ya koma aiki bayan fiye da shekara guda yana tsaye saboda matsalar wutar lantarki. Hukumar bincike ta CERN ta bayyana nasarar dawo da injin, inda daraktan gudanarwa na hajojin hanzarta zarra, Steve Myers, ya bayyana aikin gyaran da aka yi da babban ƙoƙari. CERN ta bayyana cewa an sami damar juyar da zarra nau'in proton a cikin bututun LHC mai tsawon mil 17 a ranar Juma'a, mataki mai muhimmanci kafin manyan gwaje-gwajen kimiyya su fara. Ko da yake babban aikin kimiyya bai fara ba tukuna, wannan nasarar na kawo masu bincike kusa da burinsu. An gina LHC a karkashin ƙasa a iyakar ƙasashen Switzerland da Faransa, kuma tun farkon Oktoba aka dawo da injin zuwa yanayin sanyi mai tsanani, sannan aka soma saka zarra daga baya a wancan watan. Ana sa ran gwaje-gwajen haɗa zarra masu ƙarancin ƙarfi nan da mako guda, sai kuma manyan gwaje-gwajen haɗawa mai ƙarfi su biyo a shekara mai zuwa. LHC ta fuskanci matsaloli irin na fasaha—ciki har da lokacin da tsuntsu ya jefa burodi a cikin injin, ya sanya aikin dakatawa na ɗan lokaci. Amma hukumar ta tabbatar cewa irin wannan bai jawo babbar matsala ba. Bayan samun nasarar zagayowar farko na beam a Satumba 2008, matsala ta biyo bayan gazawar haɗin lantarki a cikin ɗaya daga cikin dubban haɗin maganadiso da ke cikin injin, wanda ya haifar da lahani mai tsanani kuma ya sa aka dau lokaci ana gyara. Masana irinsu Mark Wise daga jami’ar Caltech suna da kwarin guiwa, suna kallon irin wannan ista-matsala a matsayin ɓangarorin da ake fuskanta a kowanne babban kayan aikin bincike. Sun tabbatar da cewa za a ci gaba da magance matsaloli da kuma samun ci gaba. CERN ta bayyana cewa ana sa ran LHC zai dade yana aiki har kusan shekaru ashirin ko fiye da haka, tare da fatan za a gano abubuwan kimiyya irin su Higgs boson ko tabbaci ga supersymmetry a nan gaba. Babban burin gwaje-gwajen LHC kamar ATLAS, CMS da ALICE shine tono sabbin zarra da ba a taba gani ba da kuma kwaikwayo irin yanayin da aka samu a farkon samuwar duniya bayan Big Bang, da irin sabon yanayin da ake tsammani. A cewar John Harris daga jami'ar Yale, wadannan bincike za su kai mu sabbin gurabe na binciken kimiyya, inda za a gano zarra da makamashi da suka kafa sararin samaniya.

article_content: Master & Dynamic, the premium audio brand based in New York, has introduced its latest true wireless earbuds—the MW09. This new model brings advanced features and elegant design, being the first from the brand to offer Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Sound, which delivers high-resolution audio for supported smartphones. The MW09 improves upon the previous MW08 by providing a refreshed design that’s lighter, with a more comfortable and secure fit for different ear shapes, thanks to multiple silicone and foam tip options. Users get up to 16 hours of battery life on a single charge (or 12 hours with active noise cancelation), marking a substantial upgrade for sustained listening. Company founder and CEO Jonathan Levine shared that the focus was on performance and top-quality materials. New additions include AI-driven call clarity, adaptive ANC, and enhanced app controls such as sidetone, customizable EQ, and an in-app earbud fit test. Audio quality is powered by custom 11mm beryllium drivers, delivering powerful bass, smooth treble, and clear midrange. Redesigned microphone and sensor placement ensures improved noise canceling, especially in noisy environments. Connectivity covers the latest standards: Bluetooth 5.4, LE, Auracast, and support for aptX Lossless, aptX Adaptive, and AAC codecs. While all users receive improved audio, those with Snapdragon Sound-compatible phones get the best-quality lossless music. The earbuds feature anodized aluminum with sapphire glass, and cases come in either durable Kevlar or aluminum, available in a variety of colors including black, white, gold, green, blue, and gunmetal. The sturdy charging case extends usage, and the app’s simple interface makes personalization easy. Reviewers have found the MW09 to be stylish and very comfortable, with its long battery life and detailed audio getting high marks. While the ANC is solid, it does not surpass top competitors like Sony or Bose, but overall performance and feature set make it a compelling luxury option. Prices begin at $349/€349/£319 for the aluminum case and $399/€399/£369 for the Kevlar case version. The earbuds are available to order from November 14, 2023, at masterdynamic.com, and there are several choices for materials and colors.

MW09 ya kawo sauyi da salo, yana da nauyi mai sauƙi kuma yana ba da dacewa a kunne ta yadda masu amfani za su iya zaɓar tip na silicone ko kumfa daidai da kunnensu. Sabbin fasaloli sun haɗa da kiran waya mai ƙayatarwa ta AI, ANC mai tsari, da sabuwar app da ke ba da ikon daidaita sauti, gwajin dacewar earbud da side tone. Masu duba sun yaba da salo, kwanciyar hankali a kunne, da ƙarfin batir din MW09. Ko da ANC ba ya kai Sony ko Bose ba, yana da kyau a gida. article_content: The world economy is on track for a 'soft landing' in 2024, according to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The OECD revised its forecast for global growth in 2023 to 2.9%, down slightly from its September estimate of 3.0%. For 2024, growth is expected to slow further to 2.7%, the lowest annual rate since the global financial crisis, aside from the initial year of the COVID-19 pandemic. A recovery to 3.0% growth in 2025 depends on easing inflation and continued robust growth in Asian economies. The OECD describes the global economic outlook as a moderate slowdown followed by a gradual return to normal growth rates, expecting inflation to align with central bank targets by 2025. However, the organization’s chief economist, Clare Lombardelli, cautioned that a soft landing is projected for advanced economies, but it is far from assured. The OECD also highlighted heightened geopolitical risks, particularly the Israel-Hamas conflict, as a key source of uncertainty that could slow growth and push up inflation if the situation escalates. The OECD has already forecast a temporary but notable slowdown for Israel’s economy but said the wider effects on the world economy have so far been limited. The overall global slowdown is primarily attributed to high interest rates implemented by central banks to address inflation, but growth is expected to pick up as inflation and rates decrease next year. Regionally, the OECD increased its outlook for US economic growth to 2.4% in 2023 and 1.5% in 2024, with a further rise to 1.7% in 2025. Eurozone growth is forecast at 0.6% in 2023 and 0.9% in 2024. The UK economy is expected to gradually recover, with growth rising to 0.5% this year, 0.7% in 2024, and 1.2% in 2025. Japan’s economy will likely slow to 1.0% in 2024 after growing 1.7% this year, before edging up to 1.2% in 2025. China’s growth is projected at 5.2% for 2023 but is expected to slow to 4.7% in 2024 and 4.2% by 2025, reflecting weak consumer sentiment, job market challenges, and financial stress from the real estate sector.
translated_content: Tattalin arzikin duniya na kan hanya don samun 'saukar laushi' a shekarar 2024, a cewar Kungiyar Hadin Kai da Ci Gaban Tattalin Arziki (OECD). OECD ta rage hasashen ci gaban tattalin arzikin duniya na 2023 zuwa kashi 2.9%, kasa da kashi 3.0% da ta yi a watan Satumba. A 2024, ana sa ran ci gaba zai ragu zuwa 2.7%, mafi ƙasƙanci tun bayan rikicin kuɗi na duniya, banda shekarar farko ta annobar COVID-19. Komawar ci gaba zuwa kashi 3.0% a 2025 zai dogara ne da raguwar hauhawar farashi da kuma ci gaba mai ƙarfi daga kasashen Asiya. OECD ta bayyana yanayin tattalin arzikin duniya a matsayin raguwa mai sauƙi wanda zai biyo baya da komawa ga yadda ake tafiya a da, tana sa ran hauhawar farashi zai daidaita da abin da babban bankin kasa ke so zuwa 2025. Amma babban mai bincike na OECD, Clare Lombardelli, ta gargaɗi cewa ana hasashen samun saukar laushi a kasashe masu ci gaba, to amma ba tabbas ba ne. OECD har ila yau ta jaddada babban hadari daga rikicin Isra'ila da Hamas, a matsayin muhimmin abin da zai iya rage ci gaba ko kuma saka hauhawar farashi idan wutar rikicin ta ƙara kamari. OECD ta riga ta hasashen wani dan tsaiko mai zuwa ga tattalin arzikin Isra’ila, amma har yanzu tasirin ga tattalin arzikin duniya bai karu sosai ba. Raguwa a ci gaban tattalin arzikin duniya na faruwa ne saboda karin kudin ruwa da babbar bankuna ke aiwatarwa don rage hauhawar farashi, amma ana sa ran ci gaba zai farfado yayin da hauhawar farashi da kudin ruwa suka ragu daga badi. A fannin kasashe, OECD ta kara hasashen ci gaban tattalin arzikin Amurka zuwa 2.4% a 2023 da kuma 1.5% a 2024, da 1.7% a 2025. Ci gaban yankin eurozone na kan 0.6% a 2023 da 0.9% a 2024. Kasar Birtaniya tana kara farfadowa sannu a hankali, da 0.5% bana, 0.7% a 2024 da 1.2% a 2025. Japan za ta ragu zuwa 1.0% a 2024 bayan ta kai 1.7% bana, sannan ta tashi zuwa 1.2% a 2025. Ana hasashen kasar Sin za ta samu ci gaba da kashi 5.2% a 2023, amma zai ragu zuwa 4.7% a 2024 da 4.2% a 2025, saboda rashin karfi wajen kashe kudi daga mutane, matsalar ayyukan yi, da matsalolin kudi a fannin gidaje.

article_content: Mikko Ilonen made history on Sunday by becoming the first Finnish player to win the Volvo World Match Play Championship after a determined victory over top seed Henrik Stenson at The London Club in Kent. Ilonen played impressively, recording four birdies without a single bogey despite challenging windy conditions, securing a 3&1 win and taking home the top prize of €650,000 (£515,000)—nearly double his previous largest earnings from winning the Irish Open in June. Stenson, who clinched his spot in the final with a birdie on the 18th against George Coetzee, gained an early advantage in the final with a birdie on the fourth hole. However, the world number five then faltered with a bogey on the fifth and a tee shot into the water on the eighth. Ilonen capitalized with birdies on the 10th and 12th holes, pulling three ahead. Despite trailing, Stenson showed resilience, birdieing the 13th hole to cut the deficit. On the 14th, after almost holing a chip from the back of the green, Stenson could only watch as Ilonen sank a 12-foot birdie putt to regain a three-hole lead with four holes remaining. Stenson fought back again with a two-putt birdie on the par-five 15th, but was unable to close the gap further as Ilonen—who had previously beaten Joost Luiten 2&1 in the semi-final—sealed the most significant win of his career. Ilonen, also the winner of the Irish Open earlier in the year, claimed the biggest prize of his professional career with this victory.

Ilonen ya buga wasa babba, inda ya samu birdies hudu ba tare da wani bogey ba, duk da wahalhalun iska, ya samu nasara da ci 3&1 tare da lashe babban lambar yabo ta €650,000 (£515,000)—kusan ninki biyu na mafi girman kudinsa da ya taɓa samu daga cin Irish Open a watan Yuni. Stenson, wanda ya samu gurbin karshe ne bayan yin birdie a rami na 18 da ya doke George Coetzee, ya fara da kasaita inda ya samu birdie a rami na hudu. Sai dai, lamba biyar na duniya ya yi kurma da bogey a rami na biyar sannan ya jefa kwallo cikin ruwa a rami na takwas. Ilonen ya ci gaba da birdies a ramuka na goma da goma sha biyu, ya zarce da ci uku gaba. Duk da haka, Stenson ya nuna jajircewa inda ya samu birdie a rami na 13 don rage gibi. A rami na 14, bayan kusan zai saka daga bayan green, Stenson ya kalli Ilonen yana sanya bugun birdie na kafa 12 don dawo da ci uku da saura ramuka hudu. Stenson ya yi ƙoƙarin dawowa da birdie mai bugun biyu a rami na 15 (par biyar), amma bai iya rage tazara ba yayin da Ilonen—wanda ya doke Joost Luiten 2&1 a wasan kusa da na ƙarshe—ya tabbatar da nasarar da ta fi kowacce a rayuwarsa ta wasanni. Ilonen, wanda ya ci Irish Open a farkon shekarar nan ma, ya samu mafi girman lambar yabo a aikinsa da wannan nasara.

article_content: UK Foreign Secretary William Hague is preparing to unveil a proposal for a 'red card' mechanism, which would give national parliaments the power to block EU legislation they find unacceptable. This initiative forms part of Prime Minister David Cameron's strategy to renegotiate the UK's ties with the EU prior to the 2017 referendum on membership. At present, the 'yellow card' process allows national parliaments to object to proposed EU laws, only requiring the European Commission to reconsider but not halt them. Hague contends that this does not offer sufficient control, advocating for greater authority to be returned to democratically elected national governments, who he claims are more responsive to voters than the European Parliament. He will detail the plan during his speech at the Konigswinter Conference in Germany. The government anticipates backing from other Northern European nations, notably Germany. In parallel, the Foreign Office is reviewing the allocation of powers between Brussels and member states, but specifics on which powers might be reclaimed by the UK will likely not be presented before the 2015 general election.

Wannan mataki na cikin shirin Firayi Minista David Cameron na sake tattaunawa da EU kafin zaɓen raba gardama a 2017 kan makomar Birtaniya a kungiyar. Yanzu haka, tsarin 'kati mai rawaya' yana bai wa majalisun ƙasashe damar kalubalantar dokokin EU, amma wannan ba ya hana dokar gaba ɗaya, sai dai tilasta Hukumar Tarayyar Turai ta sake tunani.
